transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Eleanor Rigby (CISO, Acme), Mark Chen (Platform Lead), Sara Lopez (Compliance)
Links referenced: https://redwood.ai/security-whitepaper (deck), shared drive: /acme/redwood-audit-sample.csv, spreadsheet: SIEM-mapping-v1.xlsx

Summary (auto): Discussed what audit logs capture, export options (SIEM, S3, webhook), retention defaults and enterprise options, KMS/HSM options for private deployment, RBAC and SSO mapping. Agreed to share sample logs and schedule a deep dive on SIEM integration.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then Priya will walk through our audit log capabilities.
[00:18] Eleanor Rigby: Thanks, Jamie. We're mainly interested in what you capture in audit logs for admin actions and API activity, and how we can export to Splunk and keep long-term retention for compliance.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Absolutely. I'll cover capture scope, export routes, retention, and encryption—and then we can talk about RBAC/SCIM mapping. Note, apologies in advance the transcript auto captions sometimes mangle product names—
[00:45] Mark Chen: No problem. Also want to know about events for model deployments, key rotation, and service account usage.
[01:02] Priya Shah: Right. At a high level audit logs capture: user auth events (SSO sign-ins, failures), admin console actions (role changes, user provisioning), API key creation/revocation, model lifecycle events (deploy, rollback, version pin), configuration changes (routing policy, retention changes), quota changes, and system operational events like autoscale and node replacements. We also log request metadata per API call: route, model id/version, tokens estimated, latency buckets, status codes.
[01:35] Eleanor Rigby: When you say request metadata, do you capture request content or PII? Our policy forbids storing raw PII in logs.
[01:44] Priya Shah: We do not persist raw request payloads in the audit log by default. Logs contain identifiers and metadata — e.g., request id, model id, route name, user id (opaque), and token counts. We can redact or hash fields on export if you need. The hosted product will exclude customer prompt text from audit events unless explicitly enabled for debugging; for Dedicated/Private you can configure more.
[02:12] Sara Lopez: Good. And retention — what's default and can we set to 7 years for regulatory reasons?
[02:20] Jamie Ortiz: Default retention for hosted is 90 days for audit logs; enterprise customers can configure retention up to multiyear via Dedicated/Private with Managed retention or by exporting to your S3/HSM before TTL. Priya, correct?
[02:33] Priya Shah: Yep. For Hosted: 90 days; for Dedicated: configurable per contract, typically 1-5 years; Private on-prem can meet whatever retention you set, including 7 years. We also support streaming exports so you can offload logs to Splunk/Datadog/Elastic/your S3 bucket before the retention window.
[02:52] Mark Chen: How do exports work? Is there a webhook or do you push to S3? We want to keep a write-once archive.
[03:01] Priya Shah: Multiple options: (1) S3 exports — batch or continuous JSONL exports; (2) Syslog or forwarders for on-prem — you can run our log forwarder to push to your SIEM; (3) direct connectors for Splunk/Datadog via HTTPS ingestion; (4) Kafka topic for stream processing; (5) webhook delivery for specific admin event hooks. For immutability, you should use S3 + WORM or your SIEM archive policy — Redwood will hand off logs; we don't enforce WORM on your side but we can sign exported bundles.
[03:34] Eleanor Rigby: For encryption, do logs at rest use customer-managed KMS? We need to ensure keys are under our control.
[03:41] Priya Shah: Yes. Hosted supports server-side encryption with Redwood-managed KMS by default. For enterprise Dedicated and Private we offer customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, or Azure BYOK) and HSM integrations for on-prem. Logs are encrypted at rest and in transit (TLS). We can also sign logs and provide checksums on export for chain-of-custody.
[04:02] Sara Lopez: And what about admin activity specifically — do you capture who did what in the console? Role changes, adding service accounts, even token rotation?
[04:11] Priya Shah: Yes—admin audit trail includes actor (user id, SSO subject), action verb (create, update, delete, rotate), target (user account, role, model id), timestamp, IP address, and a short diff for configuration changes. The diff is structural, not the full payload; sensitive fields are redacted.
[04:34] Mark Chen: Is the actor always an email? We use service principals.
[04:38] Priya Shah: The audit actor field supports SAML subject (email), service principal id, and opaque internal ids. We also capture SCIM provisioning events with group membership changes.
[04:49] Eleanor Rigby: How long do you store API key creation events? Those are sensitive.
[04:55] Priya Shah: The event is stored and the key value is never stored in plain text in the log. We store the key id and metadata. If you want, we can toggle a policy to redact key ids after X days.
[05:06] Jamie Ortiz: I'll add that we have role-based access controls integrated with SSO — if you enable SAML + SCIM, role mappings ensure only ops/admins can access audit exports.
[05:18] Sara Lopez: Do you provide fine-grained export permissions? Who can request an export?
[05:22] Priya Shah: Yes — exports require an admin+export role; you can scope to only allow exports to preconfigured endpoints. Exports show up in an export audit event too.
[05:31] Mark Chen: For SIEM integration, do you have a sample mapping? Keys -> Splunk fields?
[05:36] Priya Shah: We do — we'll share a SIEM mapping spreadsheet (JSON field map and recommended Splunk/D3 parsers). That includes field names, types, and example JSONL lines.
[05:46] Eleanor Rigby: We run Splunk with a 7-year WORM archive policy; can Redwood push daily bundles to our S3 and we handle archiving?
[05:54] Priya Shah: Yes, daily signed bundles to S3 is a common pattern. We can also stream in near real-time to your Splunk HTTP collector if you prefer.
[06:04] Jamie Ortiz: Any questions about log schema or fields you need?
[06:07] Mark Chen: One more: do you capture KV-cache flush events or incremental model cache misses? We use prefix caching in our runtimes for cost visibility.
[06:16] Priya Shah: We capture high-level runtime events: cache warm/cold signals, evictions, and autoscale events. We don't log raw cache contents. Those runtime events are useful for debugging and cost attribution.
[06:28] Sara Lopez: Auditability — can we get attestations for log retention and deletion? We need an auditable trail for when logs were purged.
[06:36] Priya Shah: Yes, deletions and TTL expirations generate audit events with retention policy id and triggering actor (system or user) and deletion timestamp. Those are retained per your retention policy.
[06:47] Eleanor Rigby: How are exports authenticated when sending to our S3?
[06:51] Priya Shah: We support cross-account roles (AWS) with assume-role principals and presigned URLs, or you can configure a bucket with a restricted put policy and provide credentials. For HTTP endpoints we support mTLS and token-based auth.
[07:05] Mark Chen: Any latency impact if we enable verbose logging?
[07:09] Priya Shah: There's a small overhead for very high-verbosity debug logging; by default audit events are asynchronous and buffered — they shouldn't affect request latency. If you enable payload capture, that increases storage and potential I/O, so we recommend dedicated pipeline for debugging.
[07:26] Jamie Ortiz: Switching gears to compliance: SOC 2/ISO. We have SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO annex info in the pack I'll share.
[07:36] Eleanor Rigby: Do you have penetration test summaries?
[07:39] Priya Shah: Yes — those are in the security package. We'll redact findings, but we share remediation timelines.
[07:45] Sara Lopez: For Private deployment, can we keep logs inside our VPC and never have them leave?
[07:51] Priya Shah: Yes — Private on-prem or VPC deployments can be configured so all logs are written to your local storage or object store. The control plane can be air-gapped if needed.
[07:59] Mark Chen: Is there a way to query audit logs via API for investigation?
[08:03] Priya Shah: We provide a read-only audit log API with query filters (actor, action, time range, resource). For large investigations we recommend exporting to your SIEM and using its query tools.
[08:15] Eleanor Rigby: What about alerts — can Redwood alert on suspicious admin activity?
[08:19] Priya Shah: We have alerting hooks and can integrate with PagerDuty/Slack/Webhook. You can set anomaly rules — e.g., sudden mass role changes, repeated failed SSO attempts, or high volume of key creation. Alerts can be delivered to your incident system.
[08:36] Mark Chen: On data residency: if we require logs to remain in EU, can we pin exports to EU S3?
[08:42] Priya Shah: Yes. Hosted regions allow EU-only storage and export endpoints in-region. Dedicated/Private gives full control.
[08:50] Sara Lopez: Are there charges for exporting logs?
[08:53] Jamie Ortiz: Export bandwidth and storage costs may apply depending on destination — we'll include cost estimates in the follow-up pricing.
[08:59] Priya Shah: Also note, egress to your S3 in the same cloud region often minimal; cross-region or high-frequency streaming has network cost implications.
[09:12] Eleanor Rigby: Can we get a sample of a redwood audit JSON line?
[09:16] Priya Shah: Yes — we'll attach a sanitized sample. Example in the sample deck: {"ts":"2026-02-17T12:01:02Z","actor":"svc-12345","action":"api_key.create","target":"key-6789","resource":"/v1/keys","ip":"x.x.x.x","meta":{"model":"rw-large-v1","route":"payments/llm"}}
[09:54] Mark Chen: Great. How do you handle log integrity? If we need to show tamper-evidence years later.
[09:59] Priya Shah: We can provide signed daily bundles (SHA256) and a chain-of-custody manifest. For high assurance we recommend S3 with object lock (WORM) + our signed manifests.
[10:14] Eleanor Rigby: For legal holds, can we pause deletions on certain days?
[10:19] Priya Shah: We can tag export bundles and apply hold flags in your S3 or with our retention policies if Dedicated.
[10:27] Jamie Ortiz: Any blockers from Acme's side to proceed?
[10:30] Mark Chen: Need to verify internal SIEM endpoints and legal retention policy. Also confirm contractual terms for Dedicated if we need longer retention.
[10:39] Eleanor Rigby: We'll also want to run a short PoC: daily export to our S3 for two weeks and validate ingestion.
[10:46] Priya Shah: Sounds good. We'll provide scripts for automation and a sample CloudFormation for cross-account role.
[10:56] Jamie Ortiz: Quick follow-up on RBAC: we support admin, billing, audit-only roles. You can create custom roles with least privilege.
[11:06] Sara Lopez: For audit-only, do they see redacted fields?
[11:10] Priya Shah: Audit-only sees metadata and diffs, but sensitive details are masked per your policy.
[11:16] Mark Chen: For SSO provisioning, does Redwood support SCIM group sync?
[11:20] Priya Shah: Yes — SCIM group sync and group-to-role mappings are supported. We can also do just-in-time provisioning.
[11:27] Eleanor Rigby: Any open vulnerabilities we should be aware of?
[11:30] Priya Shah: No critical open items; we publish our vulnerability timeline in the security pack.
[11:36] Jamie Ortiz: Ok let's recap and assign next steps.
[11:40] Priya Shah: Action items: share SIEM mapping, sample JSONL, export scripts. We'll also include SOC2 summary and retention options.
[11:50] Eleanor Rigby: Thanks. Can we get the security package and the sample logs by Tuesday?
[11:55] Jamie Ortiz: We'll target Tuesday EOD.
[12:00] Mark Chen: And we'll send our SIEM endpoints and retention policy by Friday.
[12:05] Sara Lopez: Sound good.
[12:08] Priya Shah: One small note—if you want end-to-end encryption of logs where we never see unencrypted data, Private deployment with customer-managed KMS is the path.
[12:19] Eleanor Rigby: Understood. That looks like our preferred option if we go long-term.
[12:25] Jamie Ortiz: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the technical deep dive.

End of transcript.
